integrated_description: Alex initiates a clear, emotionally honest conversation with Jordan that explicitly defines which behaviors trigger enforcement—including insults, verbal abuse, emotional dumping during attacks, and intimidation—and distinguishes permissible support (check-ins, practical help, professional referrals) from impermissible access (contact during cruel behavior). A time-limited trial period is established with immediate, stated, and escalating consequences: if mean behavior occurs, Alex ends the interaction and pauses contact for a defined period; if violations persist after the boundary is communicated, contact is progressively reduced up to and including full cutoff, with an immediate hard cutoff preserved as an unconditional right in cases of harassment or threats. Alex simultaneously secures independent support for themselves, distributes moral responsibility to Jordan as an active agent in their own change, and holds no obligation of guilt for reducing or ending contact if conditions are not met.
integration_rationale: All three stakeholders shared convergent demands for operational specificity, immediate behavioral consequences, escalation pathways, and an explicit exit option, allowing their modifications to be layered into a single coherent framework without contradiction. The only tensions—between compassion-forward framing and strict boundary enforcement—were resolved by sequencing them: compassion governs the opening conversation, while enforcement governs all subsequent conduct.
